entry.title: Injector has already been destroyed
entry.body: Injector has already been destroyed edit This error occurs when you attempt to retrieve a service from an injector that has already been destroyed. This typically happens when code tries to access dependencies after a component, directive, or module has been destroyed. Common scenarios Accessing services in callbacks after destruction When a component is destroyed, its injector is also destroyed. If an async callback later tries to access services, this error occurs: @ Component ( /* ... */ ) export class UserProfile implements OnInit { private userClient = inject (UserClient); ngOnInit () { setTimeout (() => { // ERROR: If component was destroyed before timeout fires, // the injector is no longer available this .userClient. fetchData (); }, 5000 ); } } Accessing services after unsubscribing Similar issues occur with observables if cleanup happens in the wrong order: @ Component ( /* ... */ ) export class DataView implements …

printedByTheInstalledBuild.printedAs: NG0205: Injector has already been destroyed.
printedByTheInstalledBuild.note: the digest states the title without a full stop and the build states the body with one, so a surface that renders the digest row and one that renders the message body are spelling two different strings (C2)

digest.finding: The digest states the code and the title, and its body is documentation — 943 characters, ending in an ellipsis — so it cannot stand in for the string a console prints. That string is “NG0205: Injector has already been destroyed.”, derived from the build's own throw site: the code is the throw's number printed as `NG0` + its absolute value, and the body is the literal the throw carries.

message.question: once the shipped joins have read it, which fields does a console message carry, does the stack survive, and what identifies the source?

capture.finding: The capture writes five fields per console message — `order`, `type`, `code`, `text` and `location`, the last with five of its own — and the stack survives exactly once, inside `text`, in the frame lines the message printed (C3).

consoleJoin.stackSurvivesAs: inside `text`, byte for byte: the join returns the captured string untouched, so the frames are part of the string and are never a field

lintJoin.stackDroppedAt: the first line matching `STACK_FRAME`, a newline, indentation and `at `: everything after it is dropped and the rest is trimmed

sourceIdentity.finding: Neither join carries a component, an element or a location: the console join reads only `code` and `message` out of a payload that also carries `component` and `timestamp`, and the lint join strips the stack before it names anything. What identifies a source is therefore the message body’s own words and nothing else, and the capture’s `location` — the field that really names where the message came from — is read by no join at all.

message.finding: A post-teardown NG0205 reaches the join as one finding whose fields are `text` and `code`, plus the digest’s `title`: the code is the one the message carried, the text is the message byte for byte, and no field names the component that wrote it — so the answer can state the code and the body, and must state `owner-not-in-the-message` beside them (C3, SC1).

researchRaw.finding: No record under `research/raw/` carries NG0205 as a console line: the two occurrences in the record that could state an observation are the digest enumeration M045 recorded — the generator command output that lists the 64 codes, and the digest section’s own code list — and every other record that names the code is quoting it, which is a citation and not a page hit.

producible.missing: the diagnostic was not produced on either target, and what is missing is a page action rather than a read: NG0205 is thrown by Injector.get on a destroyed injector, and neither driven page leaves a callback that performs such a lookup after its own destroy. Each target states the observable it lacks in `targets.<target>.missing`.
producible.notFabricated: No probe was run against a destroyed injector to make the code appear. A page-side call that provoked it would be the instrumentation D7 forbids, and it would report the probe rather than the page; a second leaking fixture needs its own owner ruling (plan R2). R1’s absence-only outcome is therefore the measurement, recorded as an absence with the observable it lacks.
producible.finding: The diagnostic is not producible on either target as the tree stands. What would produce it is a component whose own code calls injector.get (or a service it injected) after its injector was destroyed; the two driven pages hold no such callback, and the fixture’s stale write sets a field.

absences.notGaps: Both are states the answer renders, never a gap a capture could fill: no record this repository holds carries a per-injector handle, so no later run can add one, and the handle is not something the console stream could carry — the stream carries a code and a body, and the body names no owner.

owner-not-in-the-message.because: NG0205 prints as the code and the body “Injector has already been destroyed.” — the injector it names is the destroyed one, and no component, directive or element is named beside it
owner-not-in-the-message.finding: The one field that could name an owner is the capture’s `component`, and it is the owner of the focused element or `app-root` rather than the component that emitted the message; neither join reads it, so a joined message never carries it and the answer says `owner-not-in-the-message` instead of attributing the code to whatever was mounted last (N1, SC1).

handle-record-not-held.finding: No record this agent holds carries a per-injector handle: the three names a handle record would need occur 0 times in 38 extension modules, 136 suites and 146 `research/raw/` records, and the console stream the panel reads could not carry one — it carries a code and a body. Building one would be the page-side instrumentation D7 and SC2 forbid, so the answer states `handle-record-not-held` (C1, SC4).

absences.note: The brief this task was handed expects two `.unsubscribe(` sites; this head carries three. The two in `extension/agent-main.js` are the agent’s own subscriptions torn down on its reset path — `uninstallRouterEvents` releases the router-event subscription and `uninstallStability` the stability one — and the third is the memoised fixture loader `const CURRENCY = once(` in `scripts/stability-measure.test.mjs:288`, which releases the observable it built. None of the three is a handle the inspected page holds.
